bull_bear.body:
- **Debt-free, net cash**, but cash earmarked for (a) CY2026 refurb of 3 dehiring rigs and (b) ~$35m Jindal Pioneer vendor dues → conserving cash.
- **Dividend doubled** vs prior FY (vs the year before that) in response to shareholder concern.
- Buyback: not committed; cash prioritized for operations/refurb.
bull_bear.title: Capital Allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **ONGC concentration:** essentially single-client; revenue tied to ONGC tender cadence & pricing.
- **Day-rate / oil-price cycle:** rates "can shoot up very quickly, can crash very quickly"; India rates fell on competition in last tender.
- **Rig downtime:** dehired rigs (Jindal Pioneer, 3 in CY2026) stop earning during 3–4 month refurb.
- **Re-contracting uncertainty:** mgmt won't guide upside/downside on the 3 dehiring rigs' rehire rates.
- **Litigation:** ~INR100 cr ONGC receivable gain reversed, sub-judice in Supreme Court — no resolution timeline.
- **Competition:** GE Shipping rigs repricing FY27; competitive bidding pressure on ONGC tenders.
bull_bear.title: Risks

bull_bear.body: Measured, conservative, slightly terse. Refused to speculate on oil cycles ("leads to speculative ideas which we do not want to engage in"). Emphasized balance-sheet strength (debt-free, cash, high utilization). Mildly impatient with a repetitive analyst question on segment disclosure ("It is a very short presentation. I cannot understand why I have to explain"). Confident on global supply tightening but deliberately cautious on India rate magnitude (gradual, not a big jump).
bull_bear.title: Management Tone

bull_bear.body:
- The Q3 PAT optics are **entirely** an Other-Income reversal — operations flat. Watch for re-booking if Supreme Court rules favorably (potential future positive swing of ~INR100 cr).
- Limited international competition for ONGC is **structural**: few global rigs meet ONGC specs, and converting them is uneconomic vs India rates — a moat for Indian incumbents.
- Jindal Pioneer is in gross block but NOT yet contributing EBITDA (in refurb since ~Oct-2025) — embedded future upside once redeployed.
- Mgmt prefers India's longer 3–5 yr contracts over shorter international ones — explains domestic-first bidding even when foreign rates are higher.
bull_bear.title: Non-Obvious Points

bull_bear.body:
- Balance sheet is deleveraging and net cash: gross debt Rs 52 crore and working capital borrowing Rs 17 crore at June 26 (vs Rs 69 crore and Rs 24 crore at March 26), against liquidity available of Rs (252) crore, giving net debt / (cash) of Rs (183) crore at June 26 vs Rs (128) crore at March 26.
- Management's own framing: 'Gross debt continues to reduce' and 'Net cash position improves rapidly despite recent acquisition of rig Jindal Pioneer reflecting strong cashflows'.
- Liquidity sits almost entirely in liquid investments — Rs (248) crore of the Rs (252) crore total at June 26, with cash of only Rs (4) crore.
- Loans receivable from JV are shown as nil ('-') at both June 26 and March 26.

bull_bear.body:
- Fleet of six jack-up rigs purpose-built and maintained for Indian offshore conditions, which the Company states confers a structural advantage in meeting tender qualification criteria
- Overall fleet efficiency for FY 2025-26 of 98.55%, attributed to maintenance and operating discipline
- No Lost Time Incident recorded during the year; all five operating rigs received IADC Safety Excellence certificates, with LTI-free records ranging from two to nine years
- Operating credibility with the principal customer, evidenced by ONGC's letter of appreciation for the rig Jindal Supreme and by the award of further multi-year charters for Jindal Explorer and Jindal Pioneer
- Free of long-term debt after repaying long-term borrowings in full during the year, which the Company says affords flexibility to pursue opportunities as they arise
- Low employee turnover, with retained crews carrying forward site-specific knowledge that reinforces safety and maintenance discipline
- Regular OEM-certified equipment maintenance, in-house engineering oversight and strong vendor relationships keeping the fleet technologically current
- Demonstrated ability to acquire, refurbish and re-contract rigs, as evidenced by Jindal Pioneer
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Customer concentration - substantially the whole of revenue is derived from a single customer, ONGC — Management states revenue remains heavily concentrated with ONGC and describes a near-total dependence that concentrates commercial and pricing risk; any shift in ONGC's procurement strategy or capital allocation could disproportionately affect the Company relative to more diversified global contractors. Mitigation cited: consistent operating performance, qualification for a broad range of tenders, and maintenance of a fleet specified to the customer's technical requirements.
- Contract renewal and re-tendering risk, with three rig charters scheduled to expire during FY 2026-27 — Charters are awarded for fixed terms and are subject to competitive re-tender on expiry, with the timing of awards outside the Company's control. The pattern of tender cancellations in recent years, spanning multiple jack-up tenders across the industry, injects timing uncertainty into new contract awards. Mitigation cited: staggered contract expiries and early engagement in the tendering process; management says it is confident of redeploying the rigs under new charters.
- Day-rate risk - day rates are fixed for the contract term — Cost inflation during the term cannot be passed on, and rates on renewal are exposed to prevailing market conditions and competitive pricing behaviour. Rising costs of maintenance, OEM spares, crew retention and regulatory compliance continue to weigh on margins even as charter rates gradually recover.
- Global oversupply of jack-up rigs following large-scale rig releases by international operators — Management flags the risk of renewed rate pressure should surplus capacity migrate towards Asia-Pacific markets, which would hit the Company at the point of contract re-pricing.
- Geopolitical and supply chain risk centred on the Middle East and the Strait of Hormuz — Disruption to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz affects the movement of rigs, equipment and spares, insurance costs and mobilisation timelines, and is specifically flagged as a risk to the timely mobilisation and deployment of the rig Jindal Pioneer.
- Asset and operational risk - drilling operations are inherently hazardous and equipment-intensive — Mitigated through planned maintenance, OEM-certified servicing, class and certification compliance, and comprehensive insurance cover. The Board's report adds that operational, environmental, health and safety risks are addressed with regular monitoring, and that workplace safety remains a key priority across all operational sites.
- Human resource risk - availability and retention of qualified offshore crew — Crew availability and retention is described as critical to operations, addressed through structured training, career development and competitive terms of employment.
- Currency risk on US dollar denominated revenues and costs, alongside regulatory and compliance exposure — A portion of revenues and costs is denominated in US dollars, exposing the Company to exchange rate movements; a prudent hedging policy covers imported costs from dollar revenues. Separately, the Company is subject to an extensive framework of maritime, environmental, safety and taxation regulation and to its customer's compliance requirements. The Board's report notes that foreign exchange, interest rate, price and liquidity risks are overseen by the Risk Management Committee, whose terms of reference cover strategic, financial, operational, sectoral, sustainability (including ESG), IT and cyber security, and compliance risks.

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company's expansion in FY 2025-26 was fleet-led rather than plant-led. The fleet grew during the year with Jindal Pioneer, acquired in March 2025 and currently in the Lamprell yard in the UAE, which has secured a three-year charter from ONGC and takes the operating fleet to six jack-up rigs; management describes these assets as built and maintained specifically for Indian offshore conditions, giving a structural advantage in reliability and cost, reinforced by strong vendor partnerships and regular OEM certification. Beyond the fleet, the stated build-out is capability rather than capacity: continuous upgradation and optimum utilisation of advanced jack-up drilling rigs and offshore drilling systems, integration of digital rig monitoring and real-time tracking systems, preventive and condition-based maintenance to improve equipment reliability and maximise uptime, and training of operational personnel in collaboration with equipment manufacturers. The Company reports no technology imported in the last three financial years under any formal technology transfer agreement and nil expenditure on research and development, while continuing to use equipment and systems supplied by global OEMs. Its disclosed footprint under BRSR Section A is 22 plants/operating units and 6 offices nationally plus 1 operating unit internationally, serving 7 states in India and 1 international country, with exports nil as a percentage of turnover. No rupee capital-expenditure quantum is stated anywhere in this bundle.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Indian jack-up demand is driven principally by ONGC's exploration and development programme and its associated tendering cycle, ONGC being the single dominant demand centre in Indian waters
- Contracts are typically awarded through competitive tender for terms of three years with day rates fixed for the contract period, giving revenue visibility over the term but concentrating re-pricing risk at renewal
- Rigs purpose-built or upgraded for Indian offshore conditions, including the specifications applicable in the Mumbai High and adjoining basins, enjoy a structural advantage in meeting tender qualification criteria
- The market for rigs is expected to remain subdued over the next one to two years, after which it is expected to improve; management says the Company is well positioned to take advantage of an improvement when it occurs
- Global jack-up demand remained subdued because Saudi Aramco unwound substantially the whole of its earlier activity increase, releasing a large number of jack-up rigs whose rollover effect created an unprecedented increase in available supply
- The Indian market was substantially affected by unexpected cancellation of ONGC tenders since 2024, in certain cases after price bids had been opened, and by unexpected rate reductions from certain Indian contractors that brought charter hire rates to levels management calls unsustainable given higher operating and compliance costs
- Charter hire rates were not directly affected by the crude price movement, which management attributes to severe short-term supply disruption rather than a change in the underlying demand outlook for drilling services
- Management expects demand to improve as the cycle turns, supported by infrastructure development, energy security priorities and upstream exploration gaining attention, notwithstanding subdued tender activity over the next one to two years
- Macro backdrop cited: India's real GDP grew 7.7% in FY 2025-26 with the Reserve Bank of India projecting real GDP growth of approximately 6.6% for FY 2026-27, while global growth is projected to moderate to 3.1% in 2026
- Jindal Pioneer, acquired in March 2025 and currently at the Lamprell yard in the UAE, has secured a three-year charter from ONGC, taking the operating fleet to six jack-up rigs
- A rig was mobilised and redeployed within record time under a new charter-hire contract during the year
- Industry structure: charters in the Indian offshore jack-up market are typically awarded through competitive tender for terms of three years with day rates fixed for the contract period

thesis: Debt-free, cash-rich offshore jack-up rig operator chartering rigs to ONGC, with a non-rig services arm (directional drilling / MWD-LWD + mud logging). The investment case hinges on (a) the ONGC day-rate cycle — rates dipped in the last tender on competition but management expects gradual step-ups in upcoming tenders as Saudi Aramco recalled rigs globally (tightening international supply), and (b) redeployment of dehired/refurbished rigs (incl. newly-acquired Jindal Pioneer) at improving rates. Q3 reported PAT was optically hit ONLY by a negative Other Income — a reversal of the ~INR100 cr ONGC litigation gain booked earlier (now sub-judice in Supreme Court). Operations were unchanged QoQ.
scorecard:
> Note: This was a Q&A-heavy call with limited hard financials disclosed verbally; figures below are what management quoted on the call. Detailed P&L is in the (unread) investor presentation.

| Net debt | **Debt-free, net cash positive** | offset by ~$35m vendor dues (Jindal Pioneer) + refurb cash conservation |

**One-offs:** Negative Other Income in Q3 = **reversal of the ~INR100 cr gain** (on INR66 cr original ONGC receivable; interest + forex) booked in an earlier quarter. Bombay HC award was appealed by ONGC in Supreme Court → matter sub-judice → auditors/Board reversed the income. Purely accounting; no operational impact. No timeline on Supreme Court verdict.
guidance (critical):
- **EBITDA:** ~INR350 cr for FY26 ("slightly more than that"); ~INR350 cr again for FY27.
- **Day-rate outlook:** Expect **gradual, step-by-step** rate increases in upcoming ONGC tenders (NOT a big jump — ONGC won't accept a large jump). Last tender's rates were "not feasible." Global rates >$100k/day; Aramco recall is a positive global tailwind tightening rig supply.
- **Rig additions / redeployment:** ONGC issued a **4-rig tender** (one being bid the day of the call, 30-Jan) — Jindal Pioneer coming back into India to be bid; another ONGC tender for **4 rigs expected soon**. Aim to re-bid/secure the 3 rigs dehiring in CY2026.
- **Dry-dock / refurb cost:** INR50–100 cr **per rig**, amortized over the contract duration (not expensed upfront). Refurbishment takes ~3–4 months post-dehire.
- **Contract renewals:** 3 own rigs' contracts end in FY27 (refurb in CY2026); GE Shipping (competitor) also has 2 rigs repricing in FY27.
order book & pipeline (ongc):
- **Q4 order book: INR237 cr** (revenue-trajectory proxy).
- ONGC **4-rig tender** open — Jindal Pioneer being bid 30-Jan; expects another ~4-rig tender shortly.
- ONGC requires a **minimum 3 months' notice** before a rig dehires to bid; rigs bid as/when they dehire.
- Andaman basin: **no tenders / demand for current year**.
- International: actively pursuing (1 rig already in UAE); registered with a few clients abroad. But overseas contracts are smaller/shorter; India 3–5 yr contracts preferred → bid India first.
segment (rigs vs non-rig services):
- **Rigs (jack-up charter):** core revenue/EBITDA driver; ONGC-anchored.
- **Non-rig services:** directional drilling / MWD-LWD + mud logging. EBITDA bifurcation disclosed on Slide 10/11 of presentation (mgmt declined to scale-detail on call). Non-rig can scale without large capital deployment (asset-light vs rigs).
growth / optionality:
- **Day-rate upcycle:** Aramco recalling rigs → global tightening; few rigs match ONGC's specs → limited international competition for ONGC tenders → pricing power for incumbents.
- **Rig redeployment:** Jindal Pioneer (acquired Mar-2025, earned till Oct-2025, now in refurb) to re-contract in next few months — incremental EBITDA once redeployed (currently NOT contributing).
- **International deployment:** actively working on placing rigs abroad where rates exceed India.
- **Group-rig consolidation optionality:** earlier explored acquiring rigs from Maharashtra Seamless (MSL) — **no update / no communication received** currently.
- **Services expansion (boats/non-rig):** explored earlier; **nothing in pipeline this year** — focus is on rehiring the 3 dehired rigs.
margins & cost:
- FY26 EBITDA ~INR350 cr run-rate; margins stable operationally.
- Cost pressures: crew rates, drilling costs "increasing by the day" — feed into rate negotiations.
- Tonnage tax paid but nominal (<few lakh rupees per rig) — not material.
- Refurb cost INR50–100 cr/rig amortized over contract life (smooths P&L).
capex (rigs):
- 3 rigs dehiring in CY2026 → refurbishment (INR50–100 cr each, 3–4 months) — cash being conserved for this.
- ~$35m dues to vendor for Jindal Pioneer acquisition.
- No new-build/large fresh rig acquisition flagged; focus on refurbishing & redeploying existing fleet.
capital allocation:
- **Debt-free, net cash**, but cash earmarked for (a) CY2026 refurb of 3 dehiring rigs and (b) ~$35m Jindal Pioneer vendor dues → conserving cash.
- **Dividend doubled** vs prior FY (vs the year before that) in response to shareholder concern.
- Buyback: not committed; cash prioritized for operations/refurb.
risks:
- **ONGC concentration:** essentially single-client; revenue tied to ONGC tender cadence & pricing.
- **Day-rate / oil-price cycle:** rates "can shoot up very quickly, can crash very quickly"; India rates fell on competition in last tender.
- **Rig downtime:** dehired rigs (Jindal Pioneer, 3 in CY2026) stop earning during 3–4 month refurb.
- **Re-contracting uncertainty:** mgmt won't guide upside/downside on the 3 dehiring rigs' rehire rates.
- **Litigation:** ~INR100 cr ONGC receivable gain reversed, sub-judice in Supreme Court — no resolution timeline.
- **Competition:** GE Shipping rigs repricing FY27; competitive bidding pressure on ONGC tenders.
management tone: Measured, conservative, slightly terse. Refused to speculate on oil cycles ("leads to speculative ideas which we do not want to engage in"). Emphasized balance-sheet strength (debt-free, cash, high utilization). Mildly impatient with a repetitive analyst question on segment disclosure ("It is a very short presentation. I cannot understand why I have to explain"). Confident on global supply tightening but deliberately cautious on India rate magnitude (gradual, not a big jump).
non-obvious points:
- The Q3 PAT optics are **entirely** an Other-Income reversal — operations flat. Watch for re-booking if Supreme Court rules favorably (potential future positive swing of ~INR100 cr).
- Limited international competition for ONGC is **structural**: few global rigs meet ONGC specs, and converting them is uneconomic vs India rates — a moat for Indian incumbents.
- Jindal Pioneer is in gross block but NOT yet contributing EBITDA (in refurb since ~Oct-2025) — embedded future upside once redeployed.
- Mgmt prefers India's longer 3–5 yr contracts over shorter international ones — explains domestic-first bidding even when foreign rates are higher.
challenges → beneficiaries:
- ✅ Saudi Aramco recalling rigs globally → tighter rig supply → benefits Indian incumbents (JINDRILL) with ONGC-spec rigs (less foreign competition; rate support).
- ⭐ (none material beyond the above)

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Indian jack-up demand is driven principally by ONGC's exploration and development programme and its associated tendering cycle, ONGC being the single dominant demand centre in Indian waters
- Contracts are typically awarded through competitive tender for terms of three years with day rates fixed for the contract period, giving revenue visibility over the term but concentrating re-pricing risk at renewal
- Rigs purpose-built or upgraded for Indian offshore conditions, including the specifications applicable in the Mumbai High and adjoining basins, enjoy a structural advantage in meeting tender qualification criteria
- The market for rigs is expected to remain subdued over the next one to two years, after which it is expected to improve; management says the Company is well positioned to take advantage of an improvement when it occurs
- Global jack-up demand remained subdued because Saudi Aramco unwound substantially the whole of its earlier activity increase, releasing a large number of jack-up rigs whose rollover effect created an unprecedented increase in available supply
- The Indian market was substantially affected by unexpected cancellation of ONGC tenders since 2024, in certain cases after price bids had been opened, and by unexpected rate reductions from certain Indian contractors that brought charter hire rates to levels management calls unsustainable given higher operating and compliance costs
- Charter hire rates were not directly affected by the crude price movement, which management attributes to severe short-term supply disruption rather than a change in the underlying demand outlook for drilling services
- Management expects demand to improve as the cycle turns, supported by infrastructure development, energy security priorities and upstream exploration gaining attention, notwithstanding subdued tender activity over the next one to two years
- Macro backdrop cited: India's real GDP grew 7.7% in FY 2025-26 with the Reserve Bank of India projecting real GDP growth of approximately 6.6% for FY 2026-27, while global growth is projected to moderate to 3.1% in 2026
- Jindal Pioneer, acquired in March 2025 and currently at the Lamprell yard in the UAE, has secured a three-year charter from ONGC, taking the operating fleet to six jack-up rigs
- A rig was mobilised and redeployed within record time under a new charter-hire contract during the year
- Industry structure: charters in the Indian offshore jack-up market are typically awarded through competitive tender for terms of three years with day rates fixed for the contract period

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company's expansion in FY 2025-26 was fleet-led rather than plant-led. The fleet grew during the year with Jindal Pioneer, acquired in March 2025 and currently in the Lamprell yard in the UAE, which has secured a three-year charter from ONGC and takes the operating fleet to six jack-up rigs; management describes these assets as built and maintained specifically for Indian offshore conditions, giving a structural advantage in reliability and cost, reinforced by strong vendor partnerships and regular OEM certification. Beyond the fleet, the stated build-out is capability rather than capacity: continuous upgradation and optimum utilisation of advanced jack-up drilling rigs and offshore drilling systems, integration of digital rig monitoring and real-time tracking systems, preventive and condition-based maintenance to improve equipment reliability and maximise uptime, and training of operational personnel in collaboration with equipment manufacturers. The Company reports no technology imported in the last three financial years under any formal technology transfer agreement and nil expenditure on research and development, while continuing to use equipment and systems supplied by global OEMs. Its disclosed footprint under BRSR Section A is 22 plants/operating units and 6 offices nationally plus 1 operating unit internationally, serving 7 states in India and 1 international country, with exports nil as a percentage of turnover. moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Fleet of six jack-up rigs purpose-built and maintained for Indian offshore conditions, which the Company states confers a structural advantage in meeting tender qualification criteria
- Overall fleet efficiency for FY 2025-26 of 98.55%, attributed to maintenance and operating discipline
- No Lost Time Incident recorded during the year; all five operating rigs received IADC Safety Excellence certificates, with LTI-free records ranging from two to nine years
- Operating credibility with the principal customer, evidenced by ONGC's letter of appreciation for the rig Jindal Supreme and by the award of further multi-year charters for Jindal Explorer and Jindal Pioneer
- Free of long-term debt after repaying long-term borrowings in full during the year, which the Company says affords flexibility to pursue opportunities as they arise
- Low employee turnover, with retained crews carrying forward site-specific knowledge that reinforces safety and maintenance discipline

risks.title: Risks

- **ONGC concentration:** essentially single-client; revenue tied to ONGC tender cadence & pricing.
- **Day-rate / oil-price cycle:** rates "can shoot up very quickly, can crash very quickly"; India rates fell on competition in last tender.
- **Rig downtime:** dehired rigs (Jindal Pioneer, 3 in CY2026) stop earning during 3–4 month refurb.
- **Re-contracting uncertainty:** mgmt won't guide upside/downside on the 3 dehiring rigs' rehire rates.

non_obvious.title: Non-Obvious Points
non_obvious.body:
- The Q3 PAT optics are **entirely** an Other-Income reversal — operations flat. Watch for re-booking if Supreme Court rules favorably (potential future positive swing of ~INR100 cr).
- Limited international competition for ONGC is **structural**: few global rigs meet ONGC specs, and converting them is uneconomic vs India rates — a moat for Indian incumbents.

- Mgmt prefers India's longer 3–5 yr contracts over shorter international ones — explains domestic-first bidding even when foreign rates are higher.

strategy.body:
- Deepen the focus on domestic Indian offshore projects, using a well-maintained fleet purpose-built for Indian offshore conditions as the operational edge

themes.title: Oil & Gas - gas economy (CGD/LNG) + refining/upstream
themes.need: India's gas-economy push now collides with an outright policy reversal. ATGL grew volume 13% to 303 MMSCM and revenue 27% to INR 1,908cr, yet EBITDA FELL sequentially to INR 281cr (~14.7% margin, from INR 310cr) because the government withdrew the pooled-gas mechanism after the West Asia 'peace deal', pushing ATGL to ~15% spot volumes with Brent above $107/bbl; management also noted NWG price is 12% of the Indian crude basket, so a 62% domestic mix protects far less than it looks, and CNG station adds slowed to +5 from +25 in Q4 even as CNG demand grows ~30%. The same shock ran the other way for integrated refining: RELIANCE delivered O2C EBITDA of INR 17,000cr (+17%) THROUGH the Strait-of-Hormuz closure at 96-97% throughput while Asian peers ran 15-20% below capacity, with ethane+ROGC at ~70% of ethylene feed as distillate cracks blew out (gas oil $16 to $63, ATF $14 to $62). MGL/GUJGASLTD/IGL/IRMENERGY carry the same CGD margin squeeze; PETRONET/OIL/ONGC/IOC ride LNG-infra + domestic-gas; CHENNPETRO/MRPL ride GRM cracks; DEEPINDS/JINDRILL/SEAMECLTD on ONGC E&P capex; AEGISLOG/AEGISVOPAK add LPG/gas terminalling.
themes.driver: Whether the pooled/APM gas-allocation mechanism is restored (the single biggest CGD earnings variable); LNG spot price and Brent; GRM/distillate cracks; ONGC rig tenders & day-rates.
